Eat butter - The third step on the road to health

This is the third installment of a series of post by me on v/keto. Check out the first and second.

This was the cover of Time magazine in march 1984

Ancel Keys (se previous post) so called lipid hypothesis had finally become an indisputable fact in the medical science community in the eighties. The lipid hypothesis states that intake of saturated fat raises the amount of cholesterol in the blood which in turn leads to cardiovascular disease. Only one minor detail remained - to actually prove it. Millions of tax dollars was spent on large studies but these ambitious efforts failed to inconclusively show that this was actually true. The final nail in the coffin for the lipid hypothesis was the Whomen's Health Initiative study (WHI) that started in 1991. It showed the exact opposite of what it was supposed to prove - A diet low in saturated fat, in fact leads to more disease and a shorter life span. Since the lipid hypothesis had, and still has so many followers in the medical science community this is still controversial. A common criticism against the WHI-study is that it only showed that a low fat diet is unhealthy and did not investigate if it is unhealthy to replace saturated fat with unsaturated. However other studies have at least proved that processed vegetable fats are unhealthier than natural fats like fish, olive oil and butter. Some processed vegetable fats may lead to fewer heart attacks but that is overshadowed by the fact that they are carcinogenic and leads to an overall shorter lifespan. Studies like these are notoriously hard to carry out because they need to stretch over decades and there are many confounding factors involved. What you can do however, is to look at the real world. To avoid saturated fat has been the prevailing health message for decades now and the result is terrifying. We have an enormous health crisis on our hands. The amount of obesity, diabetes, cancer, dementia and various autoimmune diseases have exploded. You could of course contribute this to other things, like gluttony and sloth, but it find it a bit hard to believe that we suddenly have an epidemic of this mindset never before seen in history. I find it more likely that a big environmental change is to blame, and the type of foods that we eat today are vastly different compared to history.

The reporters at Time may have felt guilty when they realized what Time had been a part in in the eighties and in june last year they had a different cover page.

The wider picture is that natural animal fats keeps us humans healthy and happy and we should therefor take great care to accommodate a fair amount of these fats into our diet. To avoid fat or to replace natural animal fats with vegetable oils is one of the most damaging things we can do to our health. The worst kind of fats are the processed vegetable oils found in margarine and practically all processed food products.

The reason that processed vegetable oils are so harmful to us is that our body cannot recognize these fats for what they are - toxic. We have a a sense of smell and taste that lets us avoid natural fats of bad quality. When natural fats have oxidized, they smell and taste bad. But processed vegetable oils have been chemically altered to remove the tell tales of their oxidation. Bacteria sense this in another way, and that is the reason that cookies baked with processed vegetable oil like margarine, don't get old. The bacteria stays clear of the oxidized and toxic fats in them because they sense something we cannot.

We humans have a much larger brain than all other animals. Our large energy consuming brains have developed under hundreds of thousands of years but like all things it comes with a cost. The human brain needs plenty of energy and maintenance. And the most important substance for enabling that maintenance is fat. The fat is used to make cholesterol which is in turn used to repair and maintain the brain cells. And the high quality cholesterol - HDL, can only be made out of high quality fat which is the saturated animal kind in this case. And if we don't consume enough of this fat, our brains and body will suffer. It's plain malnutrition that it will make us sick and literally stupid in the long run. Fat and cholesterol also plays a vital part for maintaining the immune system and the endocrine system. I could continue about fat and talk about it's vital role for vitamin absorption and many other things but I'll leave it at that. I think you get the picture. One last thing though - One of the best aspects of healthy fats is that it helps with step number one. They keep us satiated and the blood sugar and insulin levels in check and thus make it much easier to avoid junk food.

So there you have it keto friends - Eat as much butter, cream, cheese, fat yougurt, lard, tallow, bacon, fish, shellfish, coconut oil, avocado and nuts as you can muster in one sitting! No need to count calories in my opinion. Just make sure those sittings are far apart (see post two).

So I had been a lurker on FPH for awhile and only recently got verified - and I considered that the pinnacle of my participation here, and I'm proud to be recognized as fit and NOT fat. Like many of you here, I have visited FPH because it's kept me motivated. Like the ancient scapegoating rituals of yore, hating the Other can provide a powerful tool for more sharply defining who you want to be both as a person and as a group of people.

I hate fatness. I hate the idea, practice, and business of being overweight or obese. I think it makes basic sense that a majority of people find obesity unattractive (aside from fetishists) and I resent the idea that I'm supposed to find fat attractive or I'm some sort of woman-hater (bullshit).

I despise the "Fat Acceptance Movement" and I think "Health At Every Size" is completely delusional horsehocky and those who push it are pushing dangerous nonsense, as the US and the rest of the industrialized world rots their insides away due to obesity-related illness the idea that it's somehow "healthy" to be huge seems to be almost criminal propaganda to be circulating to our society and our children.

That being said, I consider myself a nice, empathetic person. A large amount of the things I read here that are said about fat people I would never contemplate saying to their faces. I mean, if I found myself in a conversation with a person (fat or otherwise) who tried to propound to me the virtues of HAES or fat acceptance, I would probably firmly put them in their place if the opportunity presented itself, to at least be one additional voice in the wilderness. But I would probably completely shy away from the practice of calling them names or verbally abusing them. Just because, well, it doesn't feel nice.

All the stuff about calling fat people "fat fucks," "hamplanets," "buttergolems," etc., and the practice of "thing-i-fying" them (referring to them as things rather than people), well, I get that it gives us a common language and set of practices that keep us together as a "tribe" of sorts. But…. again…. it just ultimately doesn't feel nice to say these things, and I don't think I can sustain my participation here in part because of that, unless I can somehow justify it differently in my head….. which seems unlikely at this point, simply because of my disposition and personality.

I actually respect the philosophy of this place and many of the participants quite a lot, and I think FPH absolutely has a right to exist, and moreover, I think shame and shaming has a really critical place in society, so I still do believe that in a way, FPH serves an important function to society, but personally, I don't think I can stick around for very long. And, the doxxing, brigading stuff (I know it's officially frowned upon, but I know some of the participants here still do it), that probably is just bad and counterproductive no matter how you look at it. So, that is just something I can't get behind.

Basically, I just don't like making others feel bad, even if they are delusional, gigantic, obese, and pushing garbage like HAES and fat acceptance. I guess that's my problem with being on this sub long-term. If I wouldn't be able to stand behind what I say about people here if I was required to do so in meatspace, then maybe I shouldn't be here?

Maybe FatLogic is the place for me.

Anyways, cheers. I'll likely continue to lurk, because this place has provided me with lots of amusement and fascination over the last few months….. and again, you're doing important work by just existing.
